title: Runtime Visibility Limits of Bias Probes for Quantum Error-Mitigated Selection: code, protocol and results
description:
Code, protocol, results and paper for a preregistered fixed-budget simulation study of when a runtime bias probe can detect that a quantum error-mitigated selection decision is wrong.

Evidence type for every decision-level result: noisy simulation. Version v1.1 adds an exploratory hardware addendum, registered at OSF wh5rs with its execution package before any hardware data: one readout pair-correlation test on IBM Quantum ibm_marrakesh (51 reported QPU seconds), in which no pair came near the level at which tensored readout mitigation is worse than none (0 of 56 tests rejected). Primary endpoint on a 100-graph holdout read once: the probe rule reduced the CI-only false-certification rate, dFC = +0.0080 (95% graph-cluster bootstrap [+0.0029, +0.0142]), at a pooled coverage loss of 0.418. A registered Proposition-1 prediction test scored 45/100 hits (95% Wilson [0.356, 0.548]).

Registrations on OSF (project y7m29): protocol v3 j67wy, protocol v4 r63vn, confirmatory lock j597k, Proposition-1 predictions abuct. Large raw shot-level files are not in this archive; their SHA-256 hashes are recorded in the result JSONs.
